Rewrite the multimodal integration chapters in Python with public data (#504)

* Rewrite the multimodal integration chapters in Python with public data

Both chapters loaded their data from personal cluster paths, ran WNN
and bridge integration through R, scored methods with the deprecated
scib package, used multigrate from a git branch, and could not be
reproduced by readers.
They now run end to end in one Python environment on the NeurIPS 2021
bone marrow CITE-seq and Multiome data, which
scripts/multimodal_integration uploads from GEO (GSE194122) to lamindb
together with the GENCODE v41 GTF that GLUE needs.

Method choices follow the independent benchmarks of Hu 2024, Fu 2025
and Liu 2025 (Nature Methods): WNN via muon as the paired baseline,
totalVI for CITE-seq, MultiVI for Multiome and mosaic data, GLUE for
unpaired RNA and ATAC, and totalVI with scArches surgery for reference
mapping.
MOFA+ stays for its interpretable factors.
Embeddings are scored with scib-metrics (BRAS instead of silhouette
batch) against the unimodal embeddings, which makes the gain of each
method visible.
The advanced chapter holds out a modality or part of the data in every
example, so GLUE's label transfer (82% lineage, 63% fine types),
totalVI's protein imputation (median Spearman 0.37) and the incomplete
dataset mixing of mosaic MultiVI are all checked against measurements.

multigrate was dropped: 1.0.1 fails with anndata 0.13, and after
pinning anndata 0.12 it did not mix the CITE-seq and Multiome cells at
all in this setting, while MultiVI covers the same trimodal case.
Seurat bridge integration, MIDAS and StabMap are mentioned with their
benchmark results but not run, since bridge is R-only and MIDAS pins
anndata < 0.13 and mudata < 0.4.
pandas is pinned to 2.3 because scglue 0.4.1 writes into a read-only
array under pandas 3 copy-on-write.

The per-chapter environments are replaced by one section environment.

Closes #208 items "Multimodal paired" and "Multimodal advanced".

Signed-off-by: Lukas Heumos <lukas.heumos@posteo.net>

* Drop the pandas pin from the multimodal environment and silence warnings

scglue 0.4.1 divides a read-only Series.to_numpy() result in place in
estimate_balancing_weight, which fails under pandas 3 copy-on-write
(reported as gao-lab/GLUE#140). Instead of pinning pandas < 3, the GLUE
fit patches Series.to_numpy to return a copy for the duration of the
call, which keeps the balancing step. Skipping balancing instead lowered
label transfer from 82% to 76% (lineage) and from 63% to 58% (fine).

The ADT matrix is converted to CSC before CLR, warnings are filtered
before the imports as in the surface protein chapters, and the jax
logger is set to ERROR to drop the CUDA jaxlib message. Both chapters
were rerun under pandas 3.0.6; GLUE fine-level accuracy is now 64% and
the median totalVI protein correlation 0.34.
